final_message:
I fixed `slugify` in `src/slugify.py`, and all 5 tests in `tests/test_slugify.py` now pass.

The old version replaced each non-alphanumeric character with its own hyphen. `"  a   b  "` came out as `a---b`, and `"C++ rocks!"` came out as `c---rocks-`. The new version replaces each run of such characters with a single hyphen and strips hyphens from both ends:

```python
text = text.lower()
return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text).strip("-")
```

The extra-spaces and punctuation tests expect the cleaned output, so I think those are the "wrong results" users are seeing.

I didn't touch `truncate`, and I didn't add new tests.

Non-ASCII letters are still turned into hyphens, so `"café"` becomes `caf`. I left that alone because you didn't mention it, but I can transliterate accents if you want.
